topology: Three-router area0 point-to-point triangle with PC1 behind R1, PC2 behind R2 and HTTP SRV1 behind R3. Direct cost5 plus LAN1 gives service cost6; the backup through R2 costs21. PC2 service control costs11. Initial R1 Gi0/2 uses the wrong secret under key ID1; all routers inherit area0 MD5, so the primary pair fails while the backup still delivers traffic.
implemented: Twentieth ENARSI Layer3 Technologies entry with independent practice/reference documents, six-row addressing/authentication plan, staged instructions, working CLI reference and verification commands and current-origin/path/query permalinks. Existing layout, artwork and terminal styling are preserved.

Initial diagnosis proves three delivered requests and parent-linked replies in four host/server directions. Both PC1 and reverse server requests must use R2 at21, while PC2 retains the independent working cost11 path. Repair changes the mistyped R1 primary secret to Neighbor10 under key ID1.

Healthy design requires area0 message-digest authentication on all routers, no interface mode/key-chain override, only matching key ID1 on transits, configured/operational router IDs, passive LANs, P2P transit types, normal timers and MTU1500. Three received Full pairs, three router LSAs and LAN advertisements, intra-area O routes at AD110 with exact costs6/11 and next hops, actual HTTP service and saved configs form six live checks.

Actual fresh four-way ICMP traffic and a complete TCP-backed HTTP200 body from PC1 are observed after repair. Requests must be accepted, replies must carry matched parent IDs and requests must traverse the expected router egresses. Reading show output or configuring a route cannot manufacture proof.

Seven controlled repairs distinguish Hello/dead mismatches, a passive transit, a simple-authentication override, identical secrets with different key IDs, a null override of the area default, missing interface OSPF activation and local ExStart caused by MTU1400. Each requires real backup/control traffic while the primary is faulty and fresh four-way direct/control traffic after restoration.

Interface null authentication takes precedence over the area default. Removing the override restores inheritance. Setting both peers to null can restore forwarding but never earns authenticated health or incident credit. Explicit MD5 on both primary interfaces also cannot replace this exercise’s required area inheritance. Key-ID and type failures are checked separately from the initial wrong-key-value failure.

Removing primary OSPF activation preserves its keys, network type and cost but removes the active endpoint; reactivation must restore authenticated adjacency. MTU1400 retains physical connectivity and correct authentication but produces local ExStart with a database-description diagnostic and reciprocal backup routes at21. Peer displays may be asymmetric in the existing model; complete bilateral RFC timing/state equivalence is not claimed.

Six live and ten historical checks yield practice0/16, diagnosis1/16, baseline9/16 and full16/16. Configuration/route epochs reject stale traffic, config-only toggles and port-shutdown substitutes. YAML retains earned history while dropping runtime; a new practice attempt starts fresh and the completed reference has six live checks only.

A CLI authentication fix resolves numeric/dotted aliases of an area to one existing policy and removes an empty policy after negation. Changing or removing area0 authentication through area0.0.0.0 now affects actual peers, routes and traffic instead of creating conflicting duplicate defaults. Other area attributes are retained.

The MD5 key command now has contextual syntax for key IDs1–255, md5, the key value and key removal. Question-mark help and Tab traverse the implemented command rather than stopping after a generic word. No cryptographic MD5 wire implementation is introduced.
scope: IOS OSPFv2 authenticated-neighbor troubleshooting using area MD5 inheritance, interface simple/null overrides and explicit MD5 key IDs/values, with actual existing simulated control/data-plane delivery. Authentication uses modeled logical key compatibility, not cryptographic digest generation or wire-format interoperability. No fresh CML capture, key-chain rollover/lifetime exercise, OSPFv3 IPsec/authentication trailer exercise, full multi-area lab or complete RFC state/timing equivalence is claimed.
